summary: A target-level plan of all six exponential-sum and circle-method layers. It preserves the incoming conductor, CRT, finite differencing, Fourier, classical Waring and determinant contracts and adds the real oscillation, Burgess, function-field counting, decoupling proof inputs, optimized Waring, prime-weighted, quadratic-form, Markoff and uniform surface/statistics targets. All definitions have typed APIs and discriminating examples. Exact proof and supplier frontiers are recorded as gaps; no layer is claimed closed or formalised.

nodes.title: The bounded squared divisor factor
nodes.statement: For q>0 and natural 1≤R and r≤R, let C≥1 and suppose τ(q)≤C q^(1/(4R²)), where τ(q)=card(q.divisors). Then τ(q)^(r²)≤C^(R²) q^(1/4). All powers with nonintegral exponents are real powers.
hypotheses: q is natural and positive; R,r are natural; R≥1; r≤R; C is real and C≥1. The displayed divisor estimate is a hypothesis furnished by AN.5.
proofSteps: The positive integer q satisfies q≥1, so C q^(1/(4R²))≥1. Raise the nonnegative bound for τ(q) to r².
Since r²≤R², increase the exponent of the upper bound from r² to R², not the exponent of a base below one.
Distribute the ordinary power and use the real-power multiplication law: (q^(1/(4R²)))^(R²)=q^(1/4). R≥1 ensures the denominator is nonzero. This keeps the entire factor C^(R²).
acceptance: At R=1 and r=0 the left side is one, which is still bounded.
The restriction R≥1 prevents a zero denominator in the selected exponent.

nodes.title: Strict saving in the divisor factor
nodes.statement: Under bounded-divisor-power’s hypotheses, if q>1 and C^(4R²)<q, then τ(q)^(r²)<q^(1/2). The constant and strict threshold cannot be discarded.
hypotheses: The same q,R,r,C and divisor input as bounded-divisor-power; q>1; C^(4R²)<q.
proofSteps: Raise C^(4R²)<q to the positive real exponent 1/4. Natural-to-real power compatibility gives C^(R²)<q^(1/4).
Multiply this strict inequality by q^(1/4)>0 and combine with bounded-divisor-power.
Use q^(1/4)q^(1/4)=q^(1/2). A threshold equality gives only a non-strict conclusion from these hypotheses.
acceptance: At q=1 the asserted strict saving would read 1<1 and is false.
The arithmetic boundary C=2,R=r=1,q=16,t=4 satisfies t=Cq^(1/4), C^4=q and t=q^(1/2); it rules out strict absorption from a non-strict threshold.

nodes.title: An explicit large-conductor divisor threshold
nodes.statement: Let R≥1 and r≤R be natural and choose B∈ℕ with exp(4R²)≤B. Put C=max(1,((1/(4R²)) log 2)⁻¹)^B. For real k>max(1,(C^(4R²))^(32/7)) and positive natural q with k^(7/32)≤q, one has τ(q)^(r²)<q^(1/2).
hypotheses: R,r,B are natural; R≥1; r≤R. The displayed C is a local expression, not a new carrier or unspecified constant.
proofSteps: Take ε=1/(4R²)>0. The existing AN.5 explicit-divisor-subpower-bound, with 1/ε=4R² and the supplied B, gives τ(q)≤Cq^ε and C≥1.
From k>(C^(4R²))^(32/7), strict real-power monotonicity at exponent 7/32 gives k^(7/32)>C^(4R²). Compose with the lower bound for q.
Since k>1, the same positive power gives q>1. Invoke large-conductor-divisor-saving. B may be any certified natural upper bound.
acceptance: For R=1 the AN exponent is 1/4 and the B cutoff is exp 4.
The reciprocal exponent product (32/7)(7/32)=1 is exact; the lower modulus bound is essential.

nodes.title: One divisor threshold for the bounded factor family
nodes.statement: For every real c>0 there exists a natural K≥2 such that, for every natural k≥K, positive natural q with k^(7/32)≤q, and natural r with r<10c+2, one has τ(q)^(r²)<q^(1/2). The same K works for all permitted q and r.
hypotheses: c>0. Natural k,q,r; q>0. The factor-count hypothesis is an inequality after casting r to ℝ.
proofSteps: Choose a natural R≥max(1,10c+2) using exists_nat_ge; then every permitted r satisfies r≤R and R≥1.
Choose natural B≥exp(4R²), define C by the explicit threshold node, and choose a natural K strictly larger than max(1,(C^(4R²))^(32/7)).
For k≥K all the explicit threshold hypotheses hold. Apply large-conductor-explicit-divisor-threshold; the choices R,B,C,K depend only on c, not on q or r.
The arithmetic bounded-factor-count node supplies r<10c+2 in the source application. No squarefreeness is needed for this divisor estimate.
acceptance: For c=1 one may choose R=12 because r<12 implies r≤12.
Replacing the family by unbounded r is invalid even at a fixed positive q>1.

nodes.title: The numerical Graham–Ringrose saving factor
nodes.statement: For real k≥0, q>0, t≥0 and S, and natural r, if t≤q^(1/2) and S≤2k(t/q)^(2^(−r)), then S≤2k/q^(2^(−r−1)). This is a numerical implication; an analytic estimate for a character sum is not a conclusion.
hypotheses: k,q,t,S are real; k≥0; q>0; t≥0; r is natural. The nested exponent 2^(−r) is a real power, not natural subtraction.
proofSteps: Divide t≤q^(1/2) by q>0 to get t/q≤q^(−1/2). Both sides are nonnegative.
Raise to the positive exponent 2^(−r), then multiply by 2k≥0.
Use (−1/2)2^(−r)=−2^(−r−1) and the native negative-real-power law. In the application t=τ(q)^(r²); the antecedent S-bound must still come from the external analytic theorem with interval length k/2.
acceptance: At r=1 the resulting denominator exponent is 1/4, not 1/2.
At k=0 the implication preserves the upper bound S≤0.

nodes.title: Converting the modulus saving to the interval scale
nodes.statement: For real k>0, q≥k^(7/32), S, and natural r, the bound S≤2k/q^(2^(−r−1)) implies S≤2k^(1−(7/32)2^(−r−1)).
hypotheses: All bases are positive: k>0 and q≥k^(7/32)>0; r is natural.
proofSteps: Raise q≥k^(7/32) to the positive exponent 2^(−r−1), giving q^(2^(−r−1))≥k^((7/32)2^(−r−1)).
Use antitonicity of division by a positive denominator while retaining the nonnegative numerator 2k.
Rewrite k/k^d=k^(1−d) with d=(7/32)2^(−r−1). No integer floor is introduced into the real interval length.
acceptance: The factor 7/32 remains in the exponent; omitting it gives a stronger unsupported saving.

nodes.title: Margin above Bennett–Siksek’s stated exponent
nodes.statement: For c>0 and natural r<10c+2, put γ=2^(−10c−6) and d=(7/32)2^(−r−1). Then d>(7/4)γ. In particular the exponent margin d−γ exceeds (3/4)γ>0.
hypotheses: c is real and positive; r is natural with its stated strict real upper bound; γ and d are explicit real expressions.
proofSteps: The bound on r gives −r−1>−10c−3. Strict monotonicity of the base-two real exponential gives 2^(−r−1)>2^(−10c−3).
Write 2^(−10c−3)=8·2^(−10c−6)=8γ and multiply by 7/32.
Conclude d>(7/4)γ and subtract γ. This identifies the slack needed to absorb the factor 2; it does not suppress that factor.
acceptance: If the excluded boundary r=10c+2 is integral, the displayed comparison becomes equality d=(7/4)γ, so strictness uses the strict factor count.

nodes.title: Absorbing the remaining factor two
nodes.statement: For real k≥1, γ>0, d≥(7/4)γ and S≤2k^(1−d), if k≥2^(4/(3γ)), then S≤k^(1−γ).
hypotheses: The threshold is non-strict; the bases and exponent γ are positive. No character or modulus hypothesis is needed in this numerical lemma.
proofSteps: Raise k≥2^(4/(3γ)) to exponent 3γ/4 to obtain k^(3γ/4)≥2.
Multiply by k^(1−d)>0. The resulting power is k^(1−d+3γ/4).
Since d≥7γ/4, its exponent is at most 1−γ; monotonicity in the exponent for k≥1 proves the claim.
acceptance: At γ=1/4, d=7/16 and k=2^(16/3), the absorption comparison is equality.
At k=1 and S=2, the conclusion S≤1 fails if the threshold is removed.

nodes.title: Uniform conditional large-conductor cancellation
nodes.statement: For every c>0, put γ=2^(−10c−6). There exists a natural K≥2 such that for all natural k≥K, q>0 and r<10c+2 with k^(7/32)≤q, and every real S satisfying S≤2k(τ(q)^(r²)/q)^(2^(−r)), one has S≤k^(1−γ). The analytic inequality for S is an explicit premise, not a proved character-sum estimate.
hypotheses: Natural k,q,r; c>0; q>0; the displayed lower bound and factor-count bound. S is real; γ is local notation.
proofSteps: Take K₁ from large-conductor-eventual-divisor-saving. Choose a natural K₂≥2^(4/(3γ)), and let K=max(K₁,K₂). Positivity of γ follows from the positive base two.
For k≥K, the divisor factor is strictly below q^(1/2). Apply graham-ringrose-saving-kernel to the assumed analytic-size inequality, with t=τ(q)^(r²).
Apply large-conductor-denominator-conversion. The source exponent margin gives d≥7γ/4, and large-conductor-constant-absorption removes the factor 2.

All threshold choices depend only on c. In the intended application S is the norm of the original product-character sum over k/2<m≤k. Proving its displayed premise still requires the exact CRT character factors and the complete Graham–Ringrose proof; this theorem does not close Proposition 8.2.
acceptance: The statement keeps q and r universally quantified after K, expressing uniformity.
There is no assertion that every nonnegative S satisfies the analytic-size premise.

nodes.title: Divisor in a smooth-modulus window
nodes.statement: Let T > 1 be real and N a natural number with T ≤ N. If every prime p dividing N satisfies p ≤ T², then there is a natural divisor d of N with T ≤ d ≤ T².
hypotheses: N is automatically positive. Squarefreeness is not required for this divisor-extraction step. Bounds on natural numbers are comparisons after casting to ℝ.
proofSteps: Use strong induction on N. Since N > 1, Nat.ne_one_iff_exists_prime_dvd supplies a prime p dividing N.
If p ≥ T, choose d = p; the smoothness hypothesis gives p ≤ T².
If p < T, write N = pA with A = N div p < N. Every prime divisor of A divides N. If A ≥ T, apply the induction hypothesis to A and compose divisibility.
If A < T, then N = pA ≤ T². Choose d = N, which still satisfies N ≥ T. This proves the window without an ordering of the prime factors or a new smooth-number predicate.
acceptance: T = 3, N = 30 permits d = 6; primality of the selected block is not required.
T = 5, N = 6 permits d = N, illustrating the final induction branch.
T = 3, N = 11 has no divisor in [3,9]; the bound on prime factors cannot be dropped.

nodes.title: Pairwise-coprime bounded blocks of a squarefree modulus
nodes.statement: Let T > 1, let N be squarefree, and suppose every prime divisor p of N is at most T². There exist a list B of natural numbers and a residual integer u with 0 < u < T, u·∏B = N, every b in B in [T,T²], the entries of B pairwise coprime, and gcd(u,∏B) = 1.
hypotheses: The list and residual use the existing List, product, Squarefree and Nat.Coprime carriers. No new factorization object is defined.
N = 1 is allowed and gives B empty, u = 1. The residual may equal one. Since T > 1, every listed block exceeds one.
proofSteps: Use strong induction on N. Squarefreeness implies N ≠ 0. If N < T, take the empty list and residual N.
Otherwise extract d in [T,T²] by ES.0/smooth-divisor-window and write N = dA, A = N div d < N.
Nat.squarefree_mul_iff supplies squarefreeness of A and gcd(d,A) = 1. Prime-factor bounds pass to A, so apply the induction hypothesis to obtain A = u·∏B.

Prepend d. The product identity follows by associativity and commutativity. From gcd(d,u·∏B) = 1 obtain coprimality with u and with each member of B using Nat.coprime_list_prod_right_iff. These give pairwise coprimality of the enlarged list and coprimality of u with its product.
If N ≥ T the list cannot be empty, because the product identity would force N = u < T. Each block and the residual divide N; hence they inherit squarefreeness and, when N is odd, oddness.
acceptance: T = 3, N = 210: B = [3,5,7], u = 2 satisfies all assertions.
T = 8, N = 1: the list is empty and u = 1. No nonempty-family convention is imposed.
N = 36, T = 3 can yield [3,3,4] by unrestricted repeated extraction; pairwise coprimality fails without squarefreeness.

nodes.title: Bounded CRT modulus blocks
nodes.statement: Let T ≥ 8 and a,Q,R be natural numbers with 0 < a ≤ 8, Q and R squarefree, Q odd, Q ≥ T, gcd(Q,R) = 1 and gcd(a,QR) = 1. Suppose every prime divisor of Q or R is at most T². Then there exist q and a list B such that q divides Q, q is odd and squarefree, T ≤ q ≤ T², the product of q::B is aQR, its entries are pairwise coprime and all in (1,T²], and at most two entries of B are less than T.
hypotheses: This is a pure modulus-packing theorem. In the intended application a is the bounded 2-primary factor of the primitive conductor, Q its odd part, and R the excluded-prime product. The theorem does not prove that a given character has such a conductor decomposition.
R = 1 is explicitly permitted. Unit factors are removed. The distinguished factor comes from Q, not from the principal exclusion modulus.
proofSteps: Apply ES.0/squarefree-modulus-blocks separately to Q and R, obtaining Q = u·∏U and R = v·∏V with 1 ≤ u,v < T and every full block in [T,T²].
Since Q ≥ T, U is nonempty. Choose its first entry q. It divides Q, so inherits oddness and squarefreeness; it also satisfies the required lower and upper bounds.

Replace the primitive residual u by au. Since a ≤ 8 ≤ T and u < T, au ≤ 8T ≤ T². The principal residual v is also below T². Both are positive; no squarefreeness of a is needed because a is kept inside this single block.
Concatenate U, [au], V and [v], then delete entries equal to one. List.prod_filter_bne_one preserves the product. The first entry q remains since q ≥ T > 1.

Within each family, coprimality follows from the packing theorem. The assumptions gcd(Q,R) = 1 and gcd(a,QR) = 1 give all cross-family coprimalities and coprimality of au with the other primitive blocks. Use divisibility of each factor into its family product; filtering preserves pairwise coprimality.

Every surviving full block is at least T. Only au and v can be smaller, so after taking out the distinguished q there are at most two small entries. If R = 1, its full-block list is empty and v = 1 is deleted; no principal factor is inserted artificially.

Reindexing the resulting list by its positions provides the hypotheses of ES.0/bounded-factor-count. This gives the source's r−2 count, including an empty principal family, without replacing it by an unnecessary weaker factor bound. Character restriction and reconstruction along CRT remain a separate unclosed interface.
acceptance: T = 8, a = 4, Q = 11, R = 3 gives q::B = [11,4,3]. Both residual blocks are small: an r−1 large-block count would be false.
T = 8, a = 1, Q = 105, R = 1 permits [15,7]; the principal family contributes no factor.
T = 8, a = 1, Q = 11, R = 1 permits the one-factor list [11]. Empty maxima in the analytic threshold must then be handled by the distinguished q term alone.
A residual au = 8·7 = 56 at T = 8 lies below T² = 64; retaining the bounded a in a separate extra small block would lose the sharp two-exception count.

nodes.title: Factor count with two exceptional blocks
nodes.statement: Let k > 1, c > 0, qᵢ ≥ 1 for i in Fin r, and let E be a subset of Fin r with at most two members. Suppose qᵢ ≥ k^(7/32) whenever i is outside E, and ∏ᵢqᵢ ≤ k^(2c). Then r < 10c + 2. All inequalities and the product bound are interpreted in ℝ.
hypotheses: The exceptional set is an input identifying the at most two residual blocks from ES.0/bounded-crt-modulus-blocks. The result also permits r = 0 or 1.
Neither distinctness nor primality of the qᵢ is needed for this numerical bound. Positivity follows from qᵢ ≥ 1.
proofSteps: Each exceptional factor contributes a nonnegative logarithm. Each of the r−|E| other factors contributes at least (7/32)log k, by logarithmic monotonicity and Real.log_rpow.
Sum and use Real.log_prod. The product bound gives (r−|E|)(7/32)log k ≤ 2c log k.
Since log k > 0, divide to obtain r ≤ (64/7)c + |E| ≤ (64/7)c + 2. Because c > 0 and 64/7 < 10, the claimed strict bound follows.

The packing theorem supplies E after indexing the list; the ambient source bound aQR ∣ lcm(N₁,N₂) ≤ N₁N₂ ≤ k^(2c) is used as an inequality, never the false equality between ambient modulus and reduced period.
acceptance: For r ≤ 2 the result is consistent even if all factors are exceptional.
The coefficient is 64/7, not 32/7, because the ambient product bound is k^(2c).
Three small factors cannot be allowed: take k = 2³², c = 3/64, and q₁=q₂=q₃=2. The product is k^(2c)=8, but 3 < 10c+2 is false.

nodes.title: Interval length for the smooth-modulus estimate
nodes.statement: Let k > 2⁶⁴ be real, let 0 ≤ q ≤ k^(7/16), and let L ≤ k^(7/16). Then max(L,q^(1/4))·q^(5/4) ≤ k^(63/64) < k/2.
hypotheses: In the application L is an upper bound for the other moduli; L = 0 is allowed when there are no other factors. No character estimate is a hypothesis or a conclusion.
The first inequality only needs k > 1. The displayed combined contract uses the explicit strict threshold k > 2⁶⁴ for the second inequality.
proofSteps: Monotonicity of real powers gives q^(1/4) ≤ k^(7/64) ≤ k^(7/16), so the maximum is at most k^(7/16). Also q^(5/4) ≤ k^(35/64).
Multiply these nonnegative upper bounds and use Real.rpow_add to get exponent 7/16 + 35/64 = 63/64.
Raise k > 2⁶⁴ to the positive exponent 1/64, obtaining k^(1/64) > 2. Multiply by k^(63/64) > 0 and use the exponent sum one to get 2k^(63/64) < k.

Thus the quoted analytic theorem's lower bound R₀ is below the real interval length k/2 once the factor moduli have the stated cap. This establishes the length condition only, not the quoted estimate or its full source decomposition.
acceptance: At k = 2⁶⁴ the second comparison is equality, so the strict threshold cannot be weakened to k ≥ 2⁶⁴.
At k = 2¹²⁸ the comparison is 2¹²⁶ < 2¹²⁷.
L = 0 retains the q^(1/4) term for a one-factor decomposition; an undefined empty maximum is not used.

nodes.title: Zero-mean periodic interval remainder
nodes.statement: For f:N→C, q>0, f(n+q)=f(n) and Σ_{0≤j<q}f(j)=0, and any natural A,B, Σ_{A<m≤B}f(m)=Σ_{0≤j<(B−A) mod q}f(A+j+1). Subtraction is truncated natural subtraction.
hypotheses: No ordering assumption on A,B.
No norm bound on f is needed.
proofSteps: If B≤A, both finite index sets are empty, so conclude directly.
For B>A, use the existing natural interval enumeration m=A+j+1 with 0≤j<B−A.

The sum f(1)+...+f(q) equals the range-q sum by f(q)=f(0). Moving a length-q block one step replaces f(a+1) by f(a+q+1), which is equal by periodicity; induction gives zero for every shifted full block.
Write B−A=tq+r with 0≤r<q. Reindex the first tq entries by t blocks of length q; each block contributes zero.
In the remaining r entries, apply periodicity t times to replace f(A+tq+j+1) by f(A+j+1).
acceptance: For f(n)=(0,1,−1) indexed by n mod 3, the interval (0,2] sums to zero and (1,2] sums to −1.
When q divides B−A, the sum is zero for every starting point.
For B<A, both sides are zero; no signed-interval convention is used.

nodes.title: Norm bound by the residual interval length
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of periodic-interval-remainder, also assume ‖f(n)‖≤1 for every natural n. Then ‖Σ_{A<m≤B}f(m)‖≤((B−A) mod q), with the natural remainder cast to R.

proofSteps: Rewrite the interval sum with periodic-interval-remainder.
Apply the finite-sum triangle inequality.
Bound each of the r summands by one, and evaluate the cardinality of range r. In particular this proves a bound strictly less than q, although the exported character adapter uses the weaker ≤q.
acceptance: The χ3 table on (1,2] has norm 1 and remainder length 1, so equality occurs.
A length-q interval has bound zero, not q.

nodes.title: Incomplete nonprincipal character bound
nodes.statement: For q>0 and a nonprincipal complex Dirichlet character χ modulo q, ‖Σ_{A<m≤B}χ(m)‖≤q for all natural A,B. Values are taken by natural casting into ZMod q.
hypotheses: Nonprincipal means χ≠1 in the existing character monoid.
Neither primitive nor quadratic is assumed.
proofSteps: The character is q-periodic because q casts to zero in ZMod q.
Identify the q natural representatives 0,...,q−1 bijectively with ZMod q; use MulChar.sum_eq_zero_of_ne_one over C for the zero complete sum.
Use DirichletCharacter.norm_le_one pointwise.
Apply periodic-interval-norm; since q>0, the natural remainder is <q and hence ≤q.
acceptance: The nonprincipal character modulo 3 has values (0,1,−1), and its (1,2] sum is −1.
The principal character modulo 3 sums to 8 on (0,12], exceeding q=3.
An imprimitive but nonprincipal character is allowed; conductor need not equal q.

nodes.title: Reindexing divisible interval entries
nodes.statement: For f:N→C, natural A,B and d>0, Σ_{m∈(A,B], d|m}f(m)=Σ_{A div d<n≤B div d}f(dn), where div is natural floor division.
hypotheses: d>0 is required for injectivity and division.
Both interval endpoints are divided, and the lower endpoint remains open.
proofSteps: Map n to dn. Division with remainder gives A<dn iff A div d<n, and dn≤B iff n≤B div d.
Positive multiplication is injective, so no weight or multiplicity is introduced.
For each divisible m in the left index set, m=d(m div d); its quotient satisfies the right inequalities.
Use the finite-sum bijection. If B≤A both sides are empty because floor division is monotone.
acceptance: For f(n)=n, A=2,B=7,d=3, both sides sum 3+6=9.
For A=3,B=6,d=3, only m=6 survives; including the lower endpoint would wrongly add 3.
For A=1,B=2,d=3 there are no terms; rounding an upper endpoint upward gives a wrong term.

nodes.title: Weighted coprimality expansion
nodes.statement: For f:N→C and natural A,B,M with M>0, Σ_{A<m≤B}1_{gcd(m,M)=1}f(m)=Σ_{d|M}μ(d) Σ_{A<m≤B,d|m}f(m), with μ(d) cast from Z to C and d ranging over M.divisors.
hypotheses: M>0; no squarefreeness assumption.
The coprimality factor means f(m) if Nat.Coprime m M and zero otherwise, not a newly defined carrier.
proofSteps: For each m, gcd(m,M)>0 because M>0.
Evaluate moebius_mul_coe_zeta at gcd(m,M), use coe_mul_zeta_apply and one_apply, and obtain Σ_{d|gcd(m,M)}μ(d)=1 if gcd(m,M)=1 and zero otherwise.
A positive d divides gcd(m,M) exactly when it divides both m and M. Replace this divisor sum by the divisor set of M filtered by d|m.
Multiply by f(m), distribute and interchange the two finite sums. Coerce the integer identity to C; no infinite summability input is involved.
acceptance: M=1 retains every term, since its only divisor is 1 with μ(1)=1.
For M=4, μ(4)=0 and the expansion is still correct; squarefreeness is not needed.
M=0 is excluded: its library divisor set is empty, but the interval containing m=1 can have a nonzero coprime contribution.

Every d in M.divisors is positive by Nat.pos_of_mem_divisors; apply divisible-interval-reindex to each inner sum.
Use multiplicativity χ(dn)=χ(d)χ(n), including zero values at nonunits.
Move the fixed scalar χ(d) outside its inner finite sum and associate the factors in C.

nodes.title: Divisor-weighted character bound
nodes.statement: For q>0, nonprincipal χ modulo q, M>0, and natural A,B, ‖Σ_{A<m≤B}1_{gcd(m,M)=1}χ(m)‖≤τ(M)q, where τ(M)=card(M.divisors).

The inequality is non-strict and uniform in both endpoints.
proofSteps: Use character-exclusion-expansion and the finite-sum triangle inequality.
Each coefficient μ(d)χ(d) has norm at most one: combine abs_moebius_le_one after scalar coercion and DirichletCharacter.norm_le_one.
Apply character-interval-bound to the interval with endpoints A div d and B div d; it is valid even when that interval is empty.
There are exactly τ(M) divisor terms, each bounded by q, so their sum is at most τ(M)q.
acceptance: M=1 gives the ordinary bound q, since τ(1)=1.
For M=6 there are four divisor terms and the stated upper bound is 4q, not 2q.
τ(120)=16; the estimate makes no use of a false all-q logarithmic upper bound for τ.

nodes.title: Small-conductor square-root saving
nodes.statement: Let c>0, C≥1 and assume τ(M)≤C M^(1/(64c)) for every positive natural M. If k≥1 is natural with 8C≤k^(17/64), q>0, χ modulo q is nonprincipal, M>0, q≤8k^(7/32), and M≤k^c, then ‖Σ_{k div 2<m≤k}1_{gcd(m,M)=1}χ(m)‖≤k^(1/2). All powers in the hypotheses and conclusion are real powers of nonnegative casts.
hypotheses: The divisor estimate is an explicit hypothesis of this conditional adapter; the new unconditional supplier-instantiation nodes below import it from AN.5.
The conclusion is this small-conductor branch, not the full distinct-quadratic-character proposition.
proofSteps: Apply character-exclusion-bound to A=k div 2 and B=k.
Put ε=1/(64c)>0. Monotonicity of nonnegative real powers gives M^ε≤(k^c)^ε=k^(1/64); justify the exponent simplification using c>0 and k≥1.
The assumed divisor bound and q≤8k^(7/32) now give τ(M)q≤8C k^(15/64).
Multiply 8C≤k^(17/64) by the nonnegative k^(15/64) and use the real-power addition law: 17/64+15/64=1/2.
This proof needs no artificial split at M=k^(3/4); AN.5 supplies a uniform constant for every positive M.
acceptance: The exact exponent identity is 7/32+1/64+17/64=1/2.
For odd k=7 the index interval begins after floor(7/2)=3, so it contains 4,5,6,7.
Neither c=0 nor deletion of the lower-threshold condition is permitted; the reciprocal exponent and constant absorption need the stated hypotheses.

nodes.title: Integer evaluation of the ambient product
nodes.statement: For positive N1,N2, complex Dirichlet characters χi modulo Ni and every integer a, the existing character σ=χ1.mul χ2 modulo M=lcm(N1,N2) satisfies σ(a)=χ1(a)χ2(a).

If a is not coprime to M, choose a common prime of |a| and M. A prime divides an lcm exactly when it divides at least one input modulus, so at least one original character vanishes. The ambient character vanishes as well.
Use integer gcd via natural absolute values to cover a=0 and negative a; no division or representative choice is needed.
acceptance: Do not apply the coprime change-level formula at a nonunit.
Distinct characters of equal modulus are allowed.

nodes.title: The primitive character with its exclusion mask
nodes.statement: For every complex character σ modulo M>0 and integer a, let q=cond(σ), η=σ.primitiveCharacter and R the product of prime divisors of M absent from q. Then σ(a)=η(a) if gcd(|a|,R)=1, and σ(a)=0 otherwise.
hypotheses: No nonprincipality or primitivity hypothesis on σ; q=1 is allowed.
The mask uses coprimality of integers, equivalent to natural coprimality for nonnegative inputs.
proofSteps: If a is not coprime to R, a prime of R divides both a and M; the ambient character vanishes.
Suppose a is coprime to R. If a is also coprime to q, it is coprime to M: a hypothetical common prime of a and M either divides q or occurs among the factors of R, giving a contradiction.
In this coprime-to-M case use primitiveCharacter_apply_of_isCoprime to equate η(a) and σ(a).
In the remaining case a is not coprime to q. Since q divides M, neither character is evaluated at a unit, so both values vanish. These cases also handle a=0 and negative a.
acceptance: At M=15,q=5 the mask must remove multiples of 3 even when η is nonzero there.
At M=12 for the principal character, η is the character modulo 1 and R=6; the masked identity includes a=0.
The formula is valid for R=1; do not require a nonempty principal-factor family.

nodes.title: Cancelled primes divide both original conductors
nodes.statement: Let χ1,χ2 be primitive complex Dirichlet characters of positive moduli N1,N2. Set M=lcm(N1,N2), σ=χ1.mul χ2, q=cond(σ), and R the product of prime divisors of M not dividing q. Then R divides gcd(N1,N2).
hypotheses: Quadraticity and distinctness are unnecessary, but primitivity of both inputs is required.
proofSteps: Lift χ1,χ2 to A,B modulo M. By conductor_changeLevel and primitivity, their conductors are N1,N2.
Write A=(A·B)·B⁻¹. Apply conductor_mul_dvd_lcm_conductor and conductor_inv to obtain N1 dividing lcm(q,N2). Similarly N2 divides lcm(q,N1).
For a prime p of M not dividing q, the lcm criterion first gives p dividing at least one Ni. The corresponding reverse conductor divisibility then forces p to divide the other Ni.
Every factor of R is consequently a prime divisor of gcd(N1,N2). Its distinct-prime product divides the radical of that gcd, which divides the gcd.
acceptance: Do not infer the claim merely from q dividing M; the reverse conductor bounds are essential.
The imprimitive principal modulo 8 paired with modulo 1 is a counterexample without primitivity.
R is bounded by either original modulus, not merely by their product.

nodes.title: Quadraticity survives primitive reduction
nodes.statement: For positive N1,N2 and quadratic complex Dirichlet characters χi modulo Ni, the existing primitive product η=χ1.primitive_mul χ2 is quadratic.
hypotheses: Quadratic means the existing predicate that every value is 0, 1 or −1; it includes the principal character.
No input primitivity or distinctness is required.
proofSteps: Use the existing equivalence between quadraticity and χ²=1.
Change level to M=lcm(N1,N2); the lifts preserve squares as monoid homomorphisms, so σ²=1.
The existing change-level equality sends η to σ. Apply injectivity of changeLevel from q to M to infer η²=1, and convert back to quadraticity.
acceptance: The diagonal product may become principal and is still quadratic.

nodes.title: Distinct primitive quadratic inputs give a nonprincipal inducer
nodes.statement: For positive N1,N2, primitive quadratic complex characters χi modulo Ni, and an integer a with χ1(a)≠χ2(a), the primitive product η=χ1.primitive_mul χ2 is not principal.
hypotheses: Distinctness is as functions on integers; moduli may coincide.
The interface retains both source quadratic hypotheses; the proof only needs the second input to square to the principal character.
proofSteps: Assume η=1. Changing level to M gives A·B=1 for the two lifted inputs.
Quadraticity gives B²=1, so A=B.
Conductor invariance under changeLevel and input primitivity imply N1=N2.
Transport across this equality and apply injectivity of changeLevel to deduce χ1=χ2, contradicting the integer witness.
acceptance: Equal primitive inputs give a principal product and must be excluded.
Distinct conjugate order-three characters modulo 7 have principal product; distinctness without quadraticity is insufficient.
The χ8,χ−8 example has equal moduli and different character values, so distinct-modulus hypotheses would be too restrictive.

nodes.title: Small-conductor cancellation for the original product
nodes.statement: For each real c>0 there is a natural K≥1 such that, for every k≥K and every pair of distinct primitive quadratic complex Dirichlet characters χi of positive moduli Ni≤k^c, if q=cond(χ1.mul χ2)≤8k^(7/32), then ‖Σ_{k div2<a≤k}χ1(a)χ2(a)‖≤k^(1/2). The threshold K depends only on c.
hypotheses: Distinctness means an integer witness of different values; the moduli may be equal.
There is no prime-factor smoothness hypothesis in this small-conductor branch.
The theorem does not cover q>8k^(7/32), or assert full Proposition 8.2.
proofSteps: Choose K from eventual-small-conductor-power-saving for the same c.
Form the existing σ and η, with q>0 and η nonprincipal by primitive-product-nonprincipal.
The excluded prime product R is positive, since all its factors are positive primes (including the empty product 1). By cancelled-prime-common-support, R divides gcd(N1,N2), hence R≤N1≤k^c.
Combine ambient-product-evaluation and primitive-exclusion-evaluation, converting integer coprimality to natural coprimality at the natural interval arguments.
Apply the uniform masked-character bound with character η modulo q and exclusion modulus R. The threshold is independent of both inputs; no exponent 2c from the ambient lcm is needed.
acceptance: Preserve the quantifier order ∀c>0 ∃K ∀k,N1,N2,χ1,χ2.
The strict source Case 2 condition implies the stated non-strict bound; equality at the conductor threshold is harmless.
R=1 needs no exceptional case. Equal inputs fail the nonprincipal reduction.

nodes.title: CRT decomposition of Dirichlet characters
nodes.statement: For a finite index type I, pairwise coprime natural moduli nᵢ and a commutative monoid with zero C, put N=∏ᵢnᵢ. Define crtCharacterEquiv(n) from Dirichlet characters C of level N to families of characters C of levels nᵢ, as a multiplicative equivalence. Let E be the native unit-group CRT equivalence from (ZMod N)× to ∏ᵢ(ZMod nᵢ)×. The i-th factor has unit homomorphism u ↦ χ(E⁻¹(eᵢ(u))), where eᵢ places u in coordinate i and one elsewhere; extend by zero at nonunits using the native unit-character equivalence. The inverse multiplies the coordinate characters on CRT units and extends by zero. No new character or conductor carrier is introduced.
hypotheses: I is finite, with decidable equality for the coordinate inclusions; nᵢ are pairwise coprime. No positivity is needed for this algebraic equivalence; all conductor statements below require nᵢ>0.
C is any commutative monoid with zero. Empty I has N=1; modulus-one coordinates are allowed.
proofSteps: Compose ZMod.prodEquivPi with Units.mapEquiv and MulEquiv.piUnits to obtain E. These are existing equivalences, not additional constructions.

Compose MulChar.mulEquivToUnitHom, transport along E by MulEquiv.monoidHomCongrLeft, Pi.monoidHomMulEquiv on the finite product of unit groups, and the coordinate inverses of MulChar.mulEquivToUnitHom through MulEquiv.piCongrRight.

The native Pi.monoidHomMulEquiv supplies both inverse laws and multiplicativity. Unfold its forward map to get the single-coordinate restriction, and its inverse to get the product on units. Zero extension is inherited from MulChar.ofUnitHom.
acceptance: An empty family reconstructs the unique character modulo one, whose value is one even at zero.
A singleton family recovers its input character; at moduli 3 and 4 the principal family reconstructs a character zero at 2 and one at −1.

uses.how: Produce actual characters on the pairwise-coprime bounded blocks and recover the summand at all integers.

nodes.title: CRT reconstruction as a product of level lifts
nodes.statement: For the finite pairwise-coprime family nᵢ, N=∏ᵢnᵢ and characters φᵢ with values in a commutative monoid with zero C, crtCharacterEquiv(n)⁻¹(φ)=∏ᵢ changeLevel(nᵢ|N)(φᵢ), as characters modulo N.
hypotheses: Same finite family and coefficient assumptions as crt-character-equivalence; zero moduli and empty families are allowed here.
proofSteps: Use the unit-character equivalence to compare the two characters on units modulo N.

The inverse API gives the product of φᵢ evaluated on coordinate reductions. ZMod.prodEquivPi_apply identifies each coordinate with its native reduction; DirichletCharacter.changeLevel_toUnitHom gives exactly the same unit homomorphism for each lifted factor.
The finite product of characters agrees on units, hence agrees as a native MulChar; at nonunits zero extension is already part of the carrier.
acceptance: Empty product is the principal character modulo one.
The right side is a product after all factors are lifted to N, not the mixed-level binary mul constructor.

nodes.title: All-integer CRT reconstruction
nodes.statement: For every integer z and character χ at N=∏ᵢnᵢ with values in a commutative monoid with zero C, χ(z)=∏ᵢφᵢ(z), where φ=crtCharacterEquiv(n)(χ). No coprimality hypothesis on z is imposed.
hypotheses: I finite and the nᵢ pairwise coprime. Empty I and modulus-one coordinates are included.
proofSteps: If z is a unit modulo N, use the inverse unit formula, its inverse law, and ZMod.prodEquivPi_apply to identify every coordinate with the integer cast at nᵢ.

If z is a nonunit modulo N, transport its unit predicate across the ring CRT equivalence and use Pi.isUnit_iff. Some coordinate z modulo nᵢ is a nonunit. Both χ(z) and that factor vanish by the native MulChar nonunit law, so the product is zero.
For empty I the target product is the one-element ring; all residues are units and the empty character product has value one.
acceptance: Principal modulo 12 vanishes at 2, so reconstruction must retain nonunit zeros.
The formula applies at z=0 and z=−1; N=1 gives value one at both.

sources.locator: §8.1, proof of Proposition 8.2, printed pp.377–378; Theorem 6 on pp.376–377

nodes.title: Finite CRT products of primitive factors
nodes.statement: Let nᵢ>0 be a finite pairwise-coprime family and φᵢ native Dirichlet characters with values in a commutative monoid with zero C. If every φᵢ is primitive at nᵢ, then crtCharacterEquiv(n)⁻¹(φ) is primitive at ∏ᵢnᵢ.
hypotheses: All nᵢ>0. The index set may be empty and some nᵢ may equal one.
proofSteps: Induct over the finite index set, using crt-inverse-product to express the inverse character as a product of level lifts. The empty case is the native primitive principal character at level one.
At an insertion i, pairwise coprimality and Nat.coprime_prod_right_iff make nᵢ coprime to the product of the remaining levels. The induction hypothesis makes the remaining product primitive.

Apply the exact CA.1 primitivity-of-a-product-at-coprime-levels supplier. DirichletCharacter.changeLevel_trans identifies its two lifted factors with the full product. Reindexing and associating finite products are routine; the binary primitivity proof stays with CA.1.
acceptance: The empty family is primitive at level one.
Primitivity at level one does not require nonprincipality.
Without coprimality, squaring a nonprincipal quadratic character gives a principal product; the conclusion fails.

sources.locator: §8.1, proof of Proposition 8.2, printed pp.377–378; Theorem 6 on pp.376–377
sources.match: Finite-family adapter for the primitive factors on p.377, importing the owned binary theorem instead of rebuilding it.

nodes.title: Conductor of a finite CRT product
nodes.statement: For positive pairwise-coprime nᵢ and arbitrary characters φᵢ valued in a commutative monoid with zero C, the conductor of crtCharacterEquiv(n)⁻¹(φ) equals ∏ᵢ cond(φᵢ).
hypotheses: All nᵢ>0; neither primitivity nor nonprincipality of φᵢ is required.
proofSteps: Set dᵢ=cond(φᵢ). The native conductor_dvd_level and conductor_ne_zero give positive dᵢ dividing nᵢ. The dᵢ remain pairwise coprime by divisibility.
Take each native primitiveCharacter φᵢ and reconstruct it at D=∏ᵢdᵢ. The preceding finite primitive-family lemma makes this character primitive at D.

Its change of level from D to N equals the reconstructed original family. Expand both inverse products, use changeLevel as a monoid homomorphism and changeLevel_trans, then use changeLevel_primitiveCharacter coordinatewise.
Conductor invariance under changeLevel gives the stated exact product. This uses positive N and does not confuse dᵢ with nᵢ.
acceptance: A principal family has product conductor one regardless of its ambient moduli.
A mixture of a primitive factor modulo 4 and a principal factor modulo 3 has conductor 4 and ambient level 12.

sources.locator: §8.1, proof of Proposition 8.2, printed pp.377–378; Theorem 6 on pp.376–377
sources.match: Worker derivation making the source primitive/principal distinction precise for arbitrary CRT groupings.

nodes.title: Conductor of one CRT factor
nodes.statement: For χ of positive level N=∏ᵢnᵢ with positive pairwise-coprime nᵢ, the conductor of its i-th CRT factor equals gcd(cond(χ),nᵢ). In particular a block nᵢ dividing cond(χ) has a primitive factor; a block coprime to cond(χ) has a principal factor.
hypotheses: C is a commutative monoid with zero; every nᵢ>0. The two consequences use the native IsPrimitive and principal-character criteria.
proofSteps: Apply crt-product-conductor to the family crtCharacterEquiv(n)(χ), using the inverse law to obtain cond(χ)=∏ⱼdⱼ.
The i-th dᵢ divides nᵢ. The product of all other dⱼ is coprime to nᵢ because dⱼ|nⱼ and the nⱼ are pairwise coprime.
Split the conductor product at i and apply Nat.gcd_mul_of_coprime_of_dvd, obtaining gcd(cond(χ),nᵢ)=dᵢ.
The first consequence unfolds IsPrimitive. For a block coprime to cond(χ), dᵢ=1 and eq_one_iff_conductor_eq_one identifies its factor with the principal character.
acceptance: At ambient level 12 and conductor 4, the mod-3 factor is principal and the mod-4 factor primitive.
A principal character at a block of size greater than one is not primitive there.

sources.locator: §8.1, proof of Proposition 8.2, printed pp.377–378; Theorem 6 on pp.376–377
sources.match: Worker derivation of exactly the distinguished-factor primitivity required by Theorem 6; it also recovers the source principal factors when their moduli are coprime to the conductor.

nodes.title: Quadratic CRT factors
nodes.statement: Every CRT factor of a complex quadratic Dirichlet character is quadratic in the native MulChar.IsQuadratic sense, which includes principal characters.
hypotheses: A finite pairwise-coprime family; χ is a complex-valued native quadratic character at its product level.
proofSteps: Use MulChar.isQuadratic_iff_sq_eq_one to express quadraticity as χ²=1 in the character group.
The multiplicative equivalence sends this equality to the coordinatewise square equality. Evaluate at the selected coordinate and apply the same native criterion.
acceptance: A principal component satisfies this predicate.
No claim that all components are nonprincipal or have exact order two is made.

sources.locator: §8.1, proof of Proposition 8.2, printed pp.377–378; Theorem 6 on pp.376–377
sources.match: Worker derivation preserving the quadratic nature of the source factors without adding a new quadratic-character definition.

nodes.title: Level lifting as an exclusion mask
nodes.statement: For any natural D,R, any complex Dirichlet character η modulo D and any integer z, changeLevel(D|DR)(η)(z) equals η(z) if z and R are coprime as integers, and zero otherwise. No coprimality between D and R, and no positivity assumption, is needed for this evaluation identity.
hypotheses: Native integer evaluation and IsCoprime are used, including D=0 or R=0; analytic applications have D,R>0.
proofSteps: If z is coprime to both D and R, IsCoprime.mul_right_iff shows it is a unit modulo DR and changeLevel_eq_cast_of_dvd' gives the original value.
If z is not coprime to R, it is not coprime to DR and apply_eq_zero_iff makes the lifted value zero.
If z is not coprime to D, both η(z) and the lifted value vanish; the conditional right side is then zero in either case.
acceptance: R=1 gives equality at every integer, including nonunits modulo D.
Repeated prime factors in R do not change the mask; coprimality of D and R is unnecessary.

nodes.title: Characters on the bounded CRT blocks
nodes.statement: Let T≥8, 0<a≤8, Q odd squarefree with Q≥T, and R squarefree, with gcd(Q,R)=1 and gcd(a,QR)=1. Every prime dividing Q or R is at most T². Let η be a primitive complex character modulo aQ. There exist a natural r, positive moduli nᵢ indexed by Fin(r+1), and characters φᵢ modulo nᵢ, with: the moduli pairwise coprime and product aQR; n₀|Q, n₀ odd squarefree and T≤n₀; every 1<nᵢ≤T²; at most two indices i≠0 have nᵢ<T; cond(φᵢ)=gcd(aQ,nᵢ), so φ₀ is primitive; and η(z) times the coprimality mask for R equals ∏ᵢφᵢ(z) for every integer z.
hypotheses: The native primitive η and arithmetic hypotheses are supplied. No quadraticity is needed for this factor construction.
R=1 is allowed; all modulus-one blocks have already been discarded. Other factors need not all be primitive or principal for an arbitrary admissible grouping; their exact gcd conductors are stated.
proofSteps: Apply bounded-crt-modulus-blocks to obtain the distinguished q and the tail list B. Set r=length(B), enumerate q::B by Fin(r+1), and transfer its product, pairwise coprimality, bounds and exceptional-count properties. This is finite list indexing, not a new arithmetic packing theorem.
Lift η to aQR by native changeLevel and transport its level along the enumerated product equality. Its conductor is aQ by conductor_changeLevel and primitivity.
Apply crtCharacterEquiv to that native character. crt-component-conductor gives every gcd conductor. Since n₀|Q, it divides aQ and the distinguished factor is primitive.
Use change-level-exclusion and crt-integer-evaluation to identify the original masked summand at every integer. All nonunit zeros remain in this equality.
acceptance: For a=4,Q=11,R=1,T=8, use moduli (11,4); both factors of a primitive η modulo 44 are primitive and the principal family is empty.
For a=4,Q=11,R=3,T=8, moduli (11,4,3) exhibit two small blocks; the mod-3 factor is principal and the mod-11 factor primitive.
A singleton family has r=0; its maximum over the other moduli is the empty maximum zero in the endpoint below.

sources.locator: §8.1, proof of Proposition 8.2, printed pp.377–378; Theorem 6 on pp.376–377
sources.match: Worker assembly of the corrected source factorization, preserving the existing r−2 arithmetic bound and accepted empty-principal-family convention. General subsequent factors are permitted by the corrected Theorem 6 modulus interface.

nodes.title: Large-conductor character blocks and interval threshold
nodes.statement: Fix c>0 and a natural k>2⁶⁴. Let σ be any complex quadratic character at a positive ambient modulus M≤k^(2c), whose conductor D satisfies D≥8k^(7/32). Suppose every prime divisor of M is at most k^(7/16). Then there exist r≥0, pairwise-coprime moduli nᵢ indexed by Fin(r+1), and quadratic characters φᵢ modulo nᵢ, such that ∏ᵢnᵢ divides M, every 1<nᵢ≤k^(7/16), n₀ is odd squarefree and at least k^(7/32), φ₀ is primitive, σ(z)=∏ᵢφᵢ(z) for every integer z, and r+1<10c+2. If L=max{nᵢ:i≠0}, with L=0 for the empty set, then max(L,n₀^(1/4))n₀^(5/4)<k/2. All displayed nonintegral powers are real powers of nonnegative real casts.
hypotheses: σ need not be primitive at M. The large lower bound already excludes a principal σ.
This theorem supplies the factors and the size hypotheses for Theorem 6; it contains no character-sum estimate.
proofSteps: Set η=σ.primitiveCharacter, D=cond(σ), and R to the product of primes of M absent from D. The inherited primitive-exclusion lemmas give gcd(D,R)=1, DR|M and σ(z)=η(z) times the R mask. R is squarefree by Finset.squarefree_prod_of_pairwise_isCoprime on its finite set of distinct primes.

η is primitive by the native theorem. It is quadratic because changeLevel(η)=σ, changeLevel is injective into M>0 and a monoid homomorphism, and the square-to-one criterion descends along that injection.

Use the exact CA.1 odd-part and two-adic-conductor-bound suppliers, not their proofs: write a=2^(D.factorization(2)) and Q=D/a. Then 0<a≤8, D=aQ, Q is odd squarefree and gcd(a,Q)=1. Native ordProj_pos, ordProj_mul_ordCompl_eq_self, ordProj_dvd, not_dvd_ordCompl and coprime_ordCompl supply the elementary factor split and coprimality. From D≥8T and a≤8 obtain Q≥T for T=k^(7/32); k>2⁶⁴ gives T≥8.

Since Q|D|M and R|M, the smoothness hypotheses transfer from M; T²=k^(7/16) by Real.rpow_mul. Coprimality of D and R gives all remaining packing inputs. Apply bounded-crt-character-factors to η; its moduli multiply to DR and therefore divide M.

The native lift of η to DR is quadratic by the square criterion and changeLevel multiplicativity. crt-quadratic-components then gives all factor predicates, while the inherited mask equality identifies their product with σ at every integer.

Let the bad set be all indices with nᵢ<T. The distinguished block is not bad and the packing bound gives card(bad)≤2. The total product is at most M≤k^(2c), and all blocks are at least one. Apply bounded-factor-count to the total number r+1 to get its strict bound 10c+2.

Take the finite maximum L of all other moduli, zero if none. Its bound is k^(7/16), as is n₀. Apply graham-ringrose-interval-threshold to obtain the stated strict inequality; no analytic estimate is invoked.
acceptance: For σ=χ₁.mul χ₂ at M=lcm(N₁,N₂), the earlier ambient-product-evaluation and primitive-product-quadratic arguments give the source summand and quadraticity; M≤N₁N₂≤k^(2c), so the statement supplies Case 1 factors without assuming M=D R.
The source has r factors; this signature uses Fin(r+1), so its count is r+1 throughout.
Singleton factors use L=0. Empty principal families and conductor shrinkage at 2 remain valid.
The strict k>2⁶⁴ threshold is retained; equality would only give R₀≤k/2 from the inherited scalar bound.

nodes.statement: For every natural H and every F:ℤ→ℂ, Σ_{k=0}^{H−1}Σ_{l=0}^{H−1} F(k−l)=H F(0)+Σ_{h=1}^{H−1}(H−h)(F(h)+F(−h)), with differences in ℤ and multiplicities cast into ℂ.

nodes.title: One-step q–van der Corput estimate
nodes.statement: Suppose 1≤r≤N, a:ℤ→ℂ is r-periodic, ‖a(n)‖≤1, b vanishes outside I=(A,A+N], and ‖b(n)‖≤1 for n∈I. Put H=N div r. If T≥0 and ‖intervalCorrelation(A,N,b,hr)‖≤T for every natural 1≤h<H, then ‖Σ_{n∈I}a(n)b(n)‖²≤4Nr+2NT. All terms in this inequality are real casts; div is natural floor division.
hypotheses: A∈ℤ; N,r∈ℕ with 1≤r≤N; T∈ℝ with T≥0.
The correlation assumption retains the zero-extended finite interval; it is not a complete sum or a periodic wraparound correlation.
proofSteps: Set H=N div r. Integer division gives H≥1, Hr≤N<(H+1)r≤2Hr, and W=N+(H−1)r≤2N.
Use q-vdc-lag-bound. The pointwise bound on b and Int.card_Ioc give D≤N.
Bound each positive-lag norm by T. Gauss' finite sum formula gives 2Σ_{h=1}^{H−1}(H−h)=H(H−1). Thus the bound after dividing by H² is W(N/H+(H−1)T/H).
Use N/H≤2r, (H−1)/H≤1 and W≤2N to obtain 4Nr+2NT. These are elementary inequalities between nonnegative reals; division is legitimate because H>0.
acceptance: r=N gives H=1 and an empty correlation premise; the non-sharp 4N² bound is valid.
For N=0 or r=0 the theorem is not invoked; those cases are already covered by the undivided energy bound.

In the Polymath application a is the r-periodic factor and b is the remaining factor multiplied by its supported weight. A separate bound for C(hr) is still needed; no Weil or Graham–Ringrose estimate is hidden in T.

nodes.statement: For a natural denominator cutoff Q, reducedArcIndices(Q) is the finite set of pairs (a,q) with 1≤q≤Q, 0≤a<q and gcd(a,q)=1. Use a filtered native finite product. hypotheses: Q is natural, possibly zero. Both components are natural; a=0 is permitted only at q=1 by coprimality.
proofSteps: Filter the product of the two ranges [0,Q] by positivity, a<q and coprimality.
Extract the exact membership formula from native finite-product/filter membership.

nodes.title: Rational major arc
nodes.statement: For a pair (a,q) of natural numbers and a real radius η, majorArc((a,q),η) is the native closed metric ball of radius η about (a/q mod 1) in AddCircle(1). Only indices in reducedArcIndices(Q) are used by the circle-method family. Definition at q=0 is totalized native division, but no admissible index has q=0. proofSteps: Specialize native Metric.closedBall to the rational centre.
Use AddCircle.norm_eq after dist_eq_norm to get nearest-integer distance.
Use the native real-preimage integer-translate identity to justify the zero arc wraparound.
acceptance: The arc about zero contains points immediately below one as well as immediately above zero.
Closed boundary points belong to the arc; a negative radius gives no points.

nodes.title: Reduced rational centre separation
nodes.statement: For distinct reduced pairs (a,q),(b,r) in reducedArcIndices(Q), their torus centres have distance at least 1/(qr), and hence at least 1/Q². In particular the two centres are unequal. All divisions are real, and the positive denominators follow from membership.
hypotheses: The pairs are distinct as ordered pairs and each is reduced with numerator in [0,denominator). Q≥1 follows from nonempty membership.
proofSteps: Choose the integer translate attaining nearest-integer distance using AddCircle.norm_eq.
Multiply the translated difference a/q−b/r−z by qr to get the integer ar−bq−zqr.
This integer cannot vanish: the two reduced fractions in [0,1) would then be equal and uniqueness of reduced form would force equal pairs. Its absolute value is therefore at least one.
Divide by positive qr and use q,r≤Q.
acceptance: At Q=3 the centres 1/2 and 1/3 have distance 1/6, so a denominator-dependent positive gap is required.
Wraparound centres near zero are treated by the integer z; ordinary real distance is not substituted.

nodes.title: Major-arc separation
nodes.statement: If Q≥1, η≥0 and 2ηQ²<1, then the closed major arcs indexed by reducedArcIndices(Q) are pairwise disjoint. This is a sufficient strict size condition, not a claim of disjointness for every δ>0 in the source parametrization.
hypotheses: Arcs are closed. Strict inequality is used because two closed balls may meet at a boundary when twice the radius equals the distance of their centres.
proofSteps: If a point lies in two indexed arcs, native triangle inequality bounds the centre distance by 2η.
Reduced-centre separation gives centre distance≥1/Q², contradicting 2ηQ²<1.
For Q=⌊P^δ⌋ and η=P^(−d+δ), sufficient size is 2P^(3δ−d)<1; for any 0<δ<d/3 this holds eventually.
acceptance: For Q=2 and η=1/4 the point 1/4 lies in both the zero and half arcs; disjointness without a size condition is false.
The sufficient condition is not presented as necessary; it uses the coarse Q² bound.

nodes.title: Moment curve
nodes.statement: momentCurve(n,t) is (t,t²,…,tⁿ) in native EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), constructed by WithLp.toLp 2. Coordinate j has exponent j+1. The analytical curve is its restriction to t∈[0,1]; the polynomial map itself is defined for all real t and includes n=0.
hypotheses: n is natural; t is real. The ambient metric is Euclidean, not the native sup norm on an unwrapped Pi type.
proofSteps: Build the native Euclidean vector from the coordinate power functions.
Coordinates give continuity and smoothness. For n≥1 the first coordinate is t, so the map is injective.
acceptance: At degree two, t=2 gives (2,4), not (1,2).
At degree zero there is just the zero vector in the zero-dimensional native space.

nodes.statement: For a native Euclidean centre c, real radius R>0 and natural E, decouplingWeight(n,E,c,R)(x)=(1+‖x−c‖/R)^(−E). Positive radius and norm nonnegativity give 0<weight≤1; at the centre its value is one.
Translation of both centre and argument leaves their difference unchanged.
Only with E>n does the density have finite Lebesgue mass; boundedness alone is not integrability on the whole space.

nodes.title: Moment-curve extension operator
nodes.statement: For a real interval [a,b], complex amplitude g and x∈EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), momentExtension(n,a,b,g)(x)=∫_[a,b]g(t)exp(2πiΣ_jx_jt^(j+1))dt, using native Lebesgue measure and Bochner integration. For analytical claims g is IntegrableOn [a,b]; in the decoupling theorem it is IntegrableOn [0,1]. The source’s interval operator is an adapter to native integration, not a new Fourier transform.
hypotheses: a,b are real. If b<a the interval is empty. Integrability is exposed on continuity, norm bounds and additive APIs; the totalized native definition is not interpreted as a meaningful nonintegrable oscillatory integral.
proofSteps: Use native set integral against Lebesgue measure of a complex-valued amplitude times a unit-modulus phase.
The phase is continuous in x and t; the norm is bounded by |g(t)|, independent of x. Dominated convergence gives spatial continuity.
Finite adjacent parameter intervals partition [0,1] up to finitely many null endpoints, giving the source extension decomposition.
acceptance: At x=0 the result is exactly the amplitude integral.
The frequency starts with t, not a constant coordinate.

nodes.title: Weighted extension integrability
nodes.statement: If R>0, E>n, 1≤p<∞ and g is integrable on[a,b], then momentExtension(n,a,b,g) belongs to native MemLp at exponent p for the measure volume.withDensity(weight). Thus its eLpNorm is finite; no invalid conversion of +∞ to real zero is used.

proofSteps: Continuity of the extension gives strong measurability.
Its uniform L1 amplitude bound reduces the Lp integral to the total mass of the weight.

Split space into a radius-R ball and dyadic shells: shell j has volume bounded by a dimension constant times R^n 2^(jn), and weight bounded by a constant times2^(−jE). Sum the geometric series since E>n. Native norm-power integration and withDensity then give MemLp.

This result does not apply to E=0 in positive dimension.

nodes.title: Critical moment-curve decoupling theorem
nodes.statement: For n≥2, natural E≥100n and ε>0 there is C(n,E,ε)>0 such that for every integer M≥1, every centre c and every amplitude g integrable on[0,1], with R=M^n, ‖E_[0,1]g‖_L^{n(n+1)}(w_{c,R,E})≤CM^ε(Σ_{j=0}^{M−1}‖E_[j/M,(j+1)/M]g‖_L^{n(n+1)}(w_{c,R,E})²)^{1/2}. The norms integrate over the entire Euclidean space with weighted Lebesgue measure. C is independent of M,c,g.
hypotheses: The same E is retained in all weighted norms. Intervals are exactly the reciprocal-integer partition specified after source Theorem1.2. There is no source claim here of arbitrary noninteger partition data or automatic interpolation of every p.
proofSteps: Use the n=2 parabola decoupling base from source[9], not an unsupported assertion that this paper proves that base.

For n≥3 combine source§6 transversality/Brascamp–Lieb/plate Kakeya and ball inflation, §7 parabolic rescaling and linear–multilinear comparison, and §8 L2/lower-dimensional decoupling and the weighted iteration.
The finite recurrence in appendix§10 forces the decisive growth factor greater than one; §9 bootstraps the decoupling exponent to zero and passes to the critical endpoint.

The exact input declarations and geometric APIs for those analytic steps remain an explicit partial-stage frontier, including external proof gaps. Merely reading the whole BDG paper does not close those inputs.
acceptance: The critical exponent is n(n+1), not its half.
No theorem-bearing hypothesis record assumes the inequality; the suggested file states it as an unchecked conclusion.

nodes.title: Critical discrete restriction estimate
nodes.statement: For n≥2,E≥100n,ε>0 there is C(n,E,ε)>0 so that for N≥1, points (i−1)/N<t_i≤i/N, arbitrary complex coefficients a_i and any ball B of radius N^n, the normalized weighted L^{n(n+1)} norm of Σ_i a_i exp(2πiΣ_jx_jt_i^j) is at most CN^ε(Σ_i|a_i|²)^{1/2}. Normalized means dividing the weighted p-th-power integral by the ordinary Lebesgue volume of B, not by the weight’s total mass.
hypotheses: The ordered points lie in their separate bins but no additional uniform separation distance is assumed. Bin boundaries use the source half-open convention. The full source Theorem4.1 also covers R≳N^n and all finite p≥2; those additional target contracts remain to be split and proved.
proofSteps: Choose shrinking one-sided amplitude approximations supported inside each point’s assigned bin, including points at the right endpoint, with prescribed complex mass a_i.
Apply critical decoupling to their sum. Each interval extension is bounded by |a_i| and tends pointwise to the desired phase term.
Weighted dominated convergence is justified by integrability of w and the finite boundΣ|a_i|; the right-side weight mass divided by|B| is a constant depending only on n,E.
Let the approximation width tend to zero. The statement is the critical-radius specialization, not a claim that an arbitrary finite torus sum is bounded by this estimate.
acceptance: At critical exponent the second N-power term of source Theorem4.1 is another N^ε and is absorbed in C.
Normalization uses ordinary ball volume; a zero-radius ball is excluded by N≥1.

nodes.title: Vinogradov mean-value theorem
nodes.statement: For n≥2,s≥1 and ε>0 there exists C(n,s,ε)>0 such that for every integer N≥2, J_{s,n}(N)≤C(N^{s+ε}+N^{2s−n(n+1)/2+ε}). Here J is the concrete ordered positive-integer tuple count. Both expected terms are retained, and the real exponent in the second term is not truncated by natural subtraction.
hypotheses: The constant is uniform in N. This is an upper bound with ε loss, not an asymptotic or a local-solubility conclusion. Degree one is separate. Source n=2 arithmetic proof is only mentioned, so its use requires either a new divisor proof contract or the explicitly external n=2 decoupling base.
proofSteps: Use the discrete restriction estimate and the source Corollary4.2 Fourier-positive Schwartz majorant to bound near solutions at anisotropic tolerances N^{j−n}. Exact integer solutions form a subset; no false equivalence is used at tolerance1.
The Fourier expansion gives nonnegative terms and a uniform contribution from every counted solution, while the discrete estimate gives the two exponents.
For n≥3 the selected route includes the cubic case via decoupling induction from the parabola base; the paper title is not used as evidence excluding or establishing n=3.

For n=2 the stated endpoint is pending its actual base proof; for n=1 use the independent elementary node below. The Schwartz construction, anisotropic scaling and off-critical discrete norm contracts are still explicit proof-graph frontier tasks.
acceptance: For s=1 the exact count is N, making the N^s term indispensable.
An exponent such as2s−n(n+1)/2 may be negative and is represented with real rpow.

sources.locator: Theorem1.1 p.633; Corollary4.2 pp.638–639

nodes.title: Linear Vinogradov mean-value bound
nodes.statement: For s≥1 and all N≥0, J_{s,1}(N)≤N^{2s−1}. In degree one the only condition is equality of tuple sums, and specifying all but the final y coordinate determines that remaining coordinate uniquely. This elementary bound has constant one and no ε loss.
hypotheses: The tuples are ordered and entries are1..N. The exponent2s−1 is positive when s≥1; N=0 gives zero.
proofSteps: Project a solution to its s x-coordinates and first s−1 y-coordinates.
If two solutions have the same projection, the remaining y coordinate is equal by the one linear equation; hence the projection is injective.
Apply native finite cardinality to the2s−1 free coordinates. This uses no decoupling result.
acceptance: At s=1 the bound is equality N.
At s=2,N=3 the count is19≤27, not an unordered count.

nodes.title: Polynomial Weyl inequality
nodes.statement: For every degree d≥2 and ε>0 there is C(d,ε)>0 such that for every real polynomial f of degree d, every integer a and positive q with gcd(|a|,q)=1 and |leadingCoeff(f)−a/q|≤q^{−2}, and every N≥1, |Σ_{m=1}^Nexp(2πif(m))|≤CN^{1+ε}(N^{−1}+q^{−1}+qN^{−d})^{1/2^{d−1}}. The constant is independent of the lower coefficients, a,q,N and the leading coefficient subject to the approximation hypothesis.
hypotheses: The approximation is to the actual native leading coefficient. All powers with nonintegral exponents are real rpow; positive N,q make divisions legitimate. This classical bound is distinct from the stronger VMV-driven exponent1/[d(d−1)].
proofSteps: Expand the squared phase sum as N+2 times the sum over positive shifts of the real parts of the shifted finite phase sums; use native sum_mul_sum, unit phase modulus and conjugation. Iterate with Cauchy–Schwarz d−1 times to obtain source(9) at exponent2^{d−1}. These finite algebraic steps stay in the target proof sketch.

Fold native fwdDiff at the d−1 shifts. Binomial expansion gives the linear slope d!leadingCoeff(f) times their product; lower-degree terms become a constant. The native polynomial forward-difference theorem confirms the all-unit-step case and is not falsely used as the arbitrary-shift statement.

Each resulting finite geometric sum is at most the smaller of N and reciprocal native torus distance of its slope, with the distance-zero summand set to N. Group by the positive integer m=d!∏h. Projection to the first d−2 divisor coordinates gives at mostτ(m)^{d−2} tuples; use the exact AN.5 supplier at a smaller exponent, separating d=2 to avoid division by zero.

For |α−a/q|≤q^{-2}, a complete q-block is a permuted shifted rational grid with perturbation≤1/q. Its clipped reciprocal-distance sum is bounded by a constant times N+qlog(2q), including arbitrary starting offset and a shorter final block. If q>N^d the final desired bound follows directly from|S|≤N; otherwise log(2q) is absorbed by N to an arbitrarily small positive power.

Combine the diagonal and block contributions into N^{2^{d−1}+ε}(N^{-1}+q^{-1}+qN^{-d}); take the positive2^{d−1}-th root and renameε. All lower coefficients remain arbitrary. No additional lemma-level nodes are introduced before the breadth pass.
acceptance: For rational leading coefficient with small denominator the estimate retains q^{−1}; no uniform cancellation is asserted at every phase.
The d! product is included before grouping, and the root exponent is2^{−(d−1)}, not2^{−d}.

nodes.title: Hua mean-value inequality
nodes.statement: For each d≥2,1≤v≤d and ε>0 there is C(d,v,ε)>0 such that for every N≥1, the normalized-Haar integral on AddCircle(1) of |Σ_{m=1}^Nfourier(m^d)(α)|^{2^v} is at most CN^{2^v−v+ε}. It is a one-frequency monomial sum, not the n-dimensional full moment-curve sum and not the sharp Vinogradov critical theorem.
hypotheses: Positive entries1..N are used; d is the monomial degree and v the differencing level. The native probability Haar at period one is explicit. The allowed upper endpoint is v=d, not every v.
proofSteps: For v=1, native Fourier orthogonality and strict injectivity of m↦m^d on positive integers give the exact second moment N.

For the induction step use the non-absolute real-part differencing inequality for the monomial phase, multiply by its2^v-th absolute power and integrate; exact orthogonality converts it to a shifted-power counting problem.

With positive shifts the v-fold difference of x^d is strictly positive and strictly increasing in positive x when v<d, and divisible by every shift. Thus the fixed power-difference right side is nonzero, each shift is a divisor, and x is determined uniquely.

Import the exact AN.5 divisor subpower supplier with smaller ε to bound the positive-shift choices, giving the source recurrence. The signed differencing, monomial monotonicity/divisibility and counting calculation remain in this target-level proof sketch rather than becoming routine lemma nodes. The target remains unchecked.
acceptance: At d=2,v=2,N=2 the fourth moment is6.
Zero-inclusive sums would change the exact base count; the definition does not include m=0.

Periodicity of the phase under x→x+q identifies any complete residue interval with the source interval1..q.

nodes.title: Complete monomial sum bound
nodes.statement: For every d≥3 there is C_d>0 such that for all q≥1 and integers a with gcd(|a|,q)=1, |completePowerSum(d,q,a)|≤C_dq^{1−1/d}. The constant is independent of a and q. proofSteps: Reduce prime moduli using the gcd(d,p−1)-th-power fibre formula and the exact FF.1 Gauss/convention suppliers. Their trivial character must contribute the missing zero residue so its complete additive sum vanishes.

For prime powers use the binomial stationary phase recurrence in Lemmas6.15–6.16. For d≥3 the stated v>d range meets the required two-adic binomial threshold; the excluded d=2,p=2,v=3 case is not imported.
After reducing to exponents≤d, the normalized sum is≤1 except at finitely many primes depending only on d; at large primes the Gauss bound gives d p^{−1/6}.
CRT multiplicativity and the finite set of bad primes give one uniform C_d for all q. These are the source’s target-level proof steps; no new field Gauss theorem is planned.

The finitely many primes dividing d are included in C_d, not silently discarded.

nodes.title: Positive Waring representation count
nodes.statement: waringPositiveCount(d,s,m) is the native finite cardinality of ordered tuples x∈(Fin m)^s satisfyingΣ_i(x_i.val+1)^d=m. nodes.title: Waring counting identity
nodes.statement: For d≥1,m≤P^d, the integral over AddCircle1 of powerWeylSum(d,P,α)^s times fourier(−m)(α), with probability Haar measure, equals waringPositiveCount(d,s,m), cast to complex. proofSteps: Expand the finite product of sums and group each ordered tuple into the phaseΣx_i^d−m.

nodes.title: Monomial major-arc approximation
nodes.statement: For d≥1 there is C_d>0 such that for P≥1,q≥1, any integer a and real β, the difference between powerWeylSum(d,P,a/q+β) and q^{-1}completePowerSum(d,q,a) times∫_0^P exp(2πiβt^d)dt has norm at most C_dq(1+|β|P^d). Thus on q≤P^δ,|β|≤P^{−d+δ} it is O_d(P^{2δ}) when δ≥0.
hypotheses: No coprimality is needed for this exact residue decomposition estimate. Its sharp §9 stationary-phase refinement is a separate theorem and is not asserted here.
proofSteps: Split the positive interval into residue classes modulo q, keeping the end pieces.

On each class approximate the amplitude exp(2πiβ(qy+z)^d) by its integral. The error is bounded by endpoint norms plus integrated absolute derivative, not the defective printed quadrature bound in the notes.
The derivative integral is O_d(|β|P^d); summing q residues yields the stated error.
Collect the complete residue phase and rescale the integral variable.
acceptance: At β=0 the discrepancy is bounded by a constant times q.
No composite-modulus complete-sum cancellation follows from this approximation.

nodes.title: Classical Waring minor-arc estimate
nodes.statement: Let d≥3,s≥2^d+1 and0<δ<1/10. Put Q=floor(P^δ),η=P^{−d+δ}. There is C(d,s,δ)>0 such that for every integer P≥2, ∫_{minorArcs(Q,η)}|powerWeylSum(d,P,α)|^s dα≤CP^{s−d−δ/2^d}. The measure is probability Haar on AddCircle1.
hypotheses: The radii and denominator cutoff are explicit. Strict separation holds for sufficiently large P because3δ<d; small P are absorbed in C.
proofSteps: Dirichlet approximation provides q≤P^{d−δ}; outside the major arcs q>P^δ. Apply the polynomial Weyl bound to get a supremum P^{1−δ/2^{d−1}+ε}.
Apply Hua at exponent2^d and multiply by the supremum to power s−2^d.
Choose ε=δ/((s+1−2^d)2^d), giving a saving at least δ/2^d. Constant dependencies do not include P.
acceptance: This estimate concerns the unweighted monomial sum.
It supplies no TypeI/II or arithmetic-progression estimate for a prime-weighted sum.

nodes.title: Primitive Waring local positivity
nodes.statement: Let d≥3,s≥2d+1,p prime,d=p^τu with p∤u, and γ=τ+1 for odd p orτ+2 for p=2. IfΣ_i x_i^d=m modp^γ has a solution with at least one unit coordinate, then Reχ_{d,s,m}(p)≥p^{−γ(s−1)}>0. The hypothesis is primitive solubility at the indicated depth, not arbitrary solubility modulo p.
hypotheses: The native residues are in ZMod(p^γ). The prime-power exponent and the derivative valuation are not replaced by a nonsingularity assumption at level1 when p divides d.
proofSteps: Choose a unit coordinate and retain the other s−1 residues modulo p^γ.
The source unit-power lifting argument gives a unit d-th root at every larger depth for each of the p^{(e−γ)(s−1)} choices of the other coordinates.
Normalize the resulting lower bound on M(p^e) and use the proved local-density limit. This is a specialized monomial lifting theorem, not a duplicate general Hensel theory.
acceptance: At primes dividing d, a solution merely modulo p need not meet the stated hypothesis.
The explicit lower bound remains positive even when γ>1.

nodes.title: Uniform Waring singular-series positivity
nodes.statement: For d≥3 and s≥2^d+1 there is c(d,s)>0 such that ReS_{d,s}(m)≥c(d,s) for every natural target m. This is the classical Waring range of Theorem6.13 with its degree-two proof boundary excluded, not a claim that the mere existence of Euler factors implies positivity.

proofSteps: For every prime, source Lemma6.12 constructs a primitive solution modulo p^γ. Use the corrected γ calculation from E25 and the primitive local-positivity theorem.
For the finitely many small primes the explicit p^{−γ(s−1)} lower bounds are independent of m.
The complete monomial bound givesχ(p)=1+O_{d,s}(p^{−1−κ}) for large primes, uniformly in m with κ>0. The tail product is bounded away from zero.
Combine finite local lower bounds and the convergent Euler product.

nodes.statement: For integers d≥3 and s≥2^d+1 there exist σ(d,s)>0,C(d,s)>0 and M₀ such that for every m≥M₀, |r^+_{d,s}(m)−[Γ(1+1/d)^s/Γ(s/d)] ReS_{d,s}(m)m^{s/d−1}|≤Cm^{s/d−1−σ}. Here r^+ is the concrete ordered positive representation count. The source asserts a positive saving; no numerical optimized exponent is claimed.

The classical minor-arc theorem gives a power-saving error.
Use the major-arc approximation and binomial expansion; the total local error is O(P^{s−d−1+5δ}).

Replace the truncated series by its absolutely convergent value, and the symmetric truncated singular integral by its Gamma evaluation. Polynomial complete-sum bounds control both tails. Replace P^d by m using the actual source phase estimate corrected in E24.
Take a positive minimum of the errors’ savings and convert P-powers to m-powers. The native dominated-convergence, quadrature and beta-inversion interfaces are explicitly recorded frontiers.

nodes.statement: boundedProjectivePointCount(F,B) counts integer vectors x with |x_i|≤B_i, F(x)=0, gcd_i|x_i|=1, and first nonzero coordinate positive. nodes.title: Ternary coefficient-height alternative
nodes.statement: For every degree d≥1 there is C_d>0 such that for every primitive-coefficient integral ternary homogeneous form F of degree d irreducible over ℚ and B≥1, either N(F;B,B,B)≤d² or max|coeff(F)|≤C_dB^{d(d+1)(d+2)/2}. The height is the native supremum of coefficient absolute values on support, not an unrecorded projective or logarithmic height.
hypotheses: Primitivity is gcd of all coefficient absolute values equal to1. Irreducibility is after native coefficient extension ℤ→ℚ; it is not weakened to irreducibility over ℤ for a form with nontrivial content.
proofSteps: If there are d²+1 distinct projective representatives, form their degree-d monomial evaluation matrix with(d+1)(d+2)/2 columns.
A nonzero integer kernel vector is given by bounded minors, producing a degree-d form G with height O_d(B^{d(d+1)(d+2)/2}).

The source projective Bézout input implies G is a scalar multiple of F; coefficient primitivity bounds the height of F by that of G. The precise Bézout and kernel-minor suppliers remain explicit frontiers.

The theorem is a quantitative alternative, not a positive point asymptotic.

nodes.title: Determinant-method auxiliary hypersurface cover
nodes.statement: For n≥3,d≥2,ε>0 there are C(n,d,ε)>0 and D(n,d,ε) such that for every degree-d integral homogeneous F irreducible over ℚ, with H=max|coeff(F)|≥2, and B_i≥1, set V=∏B_i and T=max_{e∈support F}∏B_i^{e_i}. There is a finite set of integral homogeneous auxiliary forms G_j of degrees≤D, none divisible by F after native coefficient extension to ℚ, covering every primitive normalized integer zero in the box, and its cardinality is at most C(V^d/T)^{d^{−(n−1)/(n−2)}}V^ε(log H)^{2n−3}. C,D are independent of F and the B_i. For H=1 apply the theorem to2F, giving a log(2H) convention; the unmodified zero logarithm is excluded.
hypotheses: This is the exact source quantitative cover, with bounded degree and nondivisibility both essential. Irreducibility is over ℚ. No smoothness assumption on F is imposed: its singular points are handled separately.
Nondivisibility is over ℚ, not merely over ℤ: otherwise a nonprimitive scalar multiple of F would permit an auxiliary form defining the entire same hypersurface.
proofSteps: A nonzero partial derivative covers the singular points and is not divisible by F.
For nonsingular points choose O(log(HB)) primes of the required scale so every point is nonsingular modulo one of them; split by nonzero projective residue classes.

In each residue class use the source unit-derivative p-adic implicit polynomial graph, then order its monomials by degree. Column elimination forces a p-adic determinant valuationν with the source combinatorial expression.
Compare this divisibility to the archimedean determinant bound; choose a fixed degree D large enough to force all maximal minors to vanish. A bounded-degree kernel form then vanishes on the class.

Select the support monomials excluding a maximal Newton-polytope vertex multiple, ensuring F does not divide the auxiliary form. The asymptotic monomial/valuation calculation gives the stated prime scale and number of classes.
acceptance: The theorem covers points by bounded-degree proper intersections, not by forms whose degrees grow with height.
At coefficient height1 the expression log H=0 cannot be used as a cardinality bound.

nodes.statement: For degree d≥2 and ε>0 there is C(d,ε)>0 such that for every integral ternary homogeneous F of degree d irreducible over ℚ and every B_i≥1, N(F;B₁,B₂,B₃)≤CT^{−1/d²}V^{1/d+ε}. Normalize coefficient content without changing zeros. If there are at most d² points the bound is absorbed, since T≤V^d. Otherwise apply the coefficient-height alternative with the largest box size.
Absorb the resulting logarithmic coefficient dependence into a smaller chosen positive V exponent, obtaining T^{−1/d²}V^{1/d+ε}.
For equal sides T=B^d,V=B³. Choose the anisotropic ε/3 to obtain the requested cube exponent2/d+ε.

nodes.title: Van der Corput B process
nodes.statement: Fix A≥1. There is C(A)>0 such that for N,F>0, integers a<b with [a,b]⊆[N,2N], and a C⁴ real phase f satisfying F/(AN²)≤f″≤AF/N², |f‴|≤AF/N³ and |f⁽⁴⁾|≤AF/N⁴, put α=f′(a), β=f′(b) and let x_h∈[a,b] be the unique point with f′(x_h)=h. The difference between Σ_{a<m≤b}exp(2πif(m)) and Σ_{h∈ℤ∩[α,β]}exp(2πi(f(x_h)−hx_h+1/8))/√f″(x_h) has norm at most C(A)(log(2+F/N)+N/√F). Endpoint stationary terms may have full weight because their discrepancy is included in N/√F.
proofSteps: Apply truncated Poisson summation with derivative-range endpoints enlarged by one.

Use the quantitative stationary-phase estimate on interior saddle points, retain the endpoint error terms, and sum their reciprocal-distance bounds. Negative f″ follows by conjugation, with phase −1/8.

nodes.title: Burgess short-character estimate
nodes.statement: For r≥1 and ε>0 there is C(r,ε)>0 such that for every nonprincipal character χ modulo q≥2, all M∈ℤ and N≥1, |Σ_{M<m≤M+N}χ(m)|≤C N^(1−1/r) q^((r+1)/(4r²)+ε), provided q is cube-free or r≤3. nodes.title: Conditional Jacobi progression estimate
nodes.statement: Assume shortCharacterHypothesis(n,δ). For every ε>0 there is C(n,δ,ε)>0 such that for every odd squarefree q>1, its primitive quadratic character χ_q, every nonzero integer k with q∤k, every l,M∈ℤ and 1≤N≤q^(1/n), |Σ_{M<m≤M+N, k∣m−l}χ_q(m)|≤C q^((1−δ)/n+ε). The constant is uniform in k,l,M. This ε-loss version retains the same δ. Shrinking δ absorbs ε to recover a fixed positive saving, as in the quoted corollary.
proofSteps: Let d=gcd(k,q). If d∤l the progression imposes fixed nonzero residue classes at primes dividing d; if d∣l it forces χ_q to vanish at those primes.

In the nonzero case remove the fixed prime factors and apply C_n to the remaining nonprincipal squarefree character modulo q/d and the reindexed interval, using Q=q. Squarefreeness and q∤k ensure q/d>1. Bound the fixed factors by one.

nodes.title: Critical discrete decoupling for the sparse monomial curve
nodes.statement: For integers1≤t≤k and ε>0, let γ(u)=(u^k,u^{t−1},…,u),u∈[1,2]. Letσ be the geometric affine dimension of {∇F=0}; if n−σ>(d−1)2^d, then for a fixed bounded coordinate boxB and P→∞, the zero-fiber count has asymptotic σ∞(F,B)(∏_pσ_p(F,0))P^{n−d}+O_{F,B}(P^{n−d−δ}),δ>0. The series and oscillatory integral converge absolutely. A nonsingular real zero in the interior ofB and nonsingular integralp-adic zeros for everyp make the main coefficient positive and give a nonzero integral zero for largeP. nodes.title: Binary-form value and collision bounds
nodes.statement: LetG∈ℤ[X,Y] be a fixed homogeneous binary form of degreed≥3 with no geometric linear factor of multiplicity≥d/2 andG(1,0)>0. Its rational linear symmetry group is finite of order≤d·d!. The number of positive integersm≤X represented byG is bounded above and below by positiveG-dependent multiples ofX^{2/d}. For everyε>0 at mostC(G,ε)X^{52/(1+26d)+ε} have two inequivalent integral representations in binaryFormEquivalent. Constants depend onG and may be ineffective through Roth. This supplies the analytic transfer to arithmetic statistics, without re-planning a generic statistical framework.
proofSteps: Count the tails of integral representations near roots using Roth’s exact lower-bound form and primitive lattice strips; obtainΣr_tail≤X^{1/d}logX+(X/C)^{2/(d−1)}.

The collision surfaceG(x₁,x₂)−G(x₃,x₄)=0 has no linear/quadratic rational factor under the multiplicity hypothesis. Its line-free points are controlled by the surface theorem; rational symmetry lines give equivalent representations.
BalanceC^{52/27} with(X/C)^{2/(d−1)} atC=X^{27/(1+26d)}. Positive area and Cauchy–Schwarz give the represented-value lower bound.
The symmetry group acts faithfully on the≥3 geometric roots modulo scalar d-th roots of unity, giving order≤d·d!.
